project: cellular-gaits — embodied escape (WP-D bundle for WP-E)
summary: Looming -> the real FlyWire connectome (LC4/LPLC2 -> DNp01 Giant Fiber) -> an embodied NeuroMechFly escape, precomputed for in-browser replay. Three conditions share env seed + warm-up so they diverge only at looming onset.

files.flee_left.mp4: left-threat escape clip (body bolts right, away)
files.flee_right.mp4: right-threat escape clip (body turns left, away)

trace_fields.brain: per sync-window (window_step, t_s, loom_L/R, hz_L/R, dnp01_mean/L/R, drive, bearing_deg); baseline is flat zero
trace_fields.body: per control step (t_s, thorax_xy, thorax_z, yaw_deg)
trace_fields.summary: gf_peak_hz, drive_peak, displacement, heading_change_deg, turn_vs_baseline_deg {60ms,100ms,160ms,200ms} (the escape signature: unwrapped turn vs the no-threat baseline; left threat negative=bolts right, right threat positive=turns left), threat_min_dist, threat_hit

caveats: Not a calibrated escape threshold: the isolated Giant Fiber saturates (no whole-brain inhibition). The claim is 'the real connectome routes a looming cue to an embodied escape', not selectivity.
The left-strong / right-weak escape asymmetry is the X-A body controller's, inherited and reported, not a new artifact.
Three interface mappings (loom->Hz, DNp01->drive, 15 ms sync) are hand-chosen knobs; one descending neuron stands in for the whole escape command; the looming front-end is a hand-built stand-in.
